UPSTREAM: gpio / ACPI: ignore GpioInt() GPIOs when requesting GPIO_OUT_* When firmware does not use _DSD properties that allow properly name GPIO resources, the kernel falls back on parsing _CRS resources, and will return entries described as GpioInt() as general purpose GPIOs even though they are meant to be used simply as interrupt sources for the device: Device (ETSA) { Name (_HID, "ELAN0001") ... Method(_CRS, 0x0, NotSerialized) { Name(BUF0,ResourceTemplate () { I2CSerialBus( 0x10, /* SlaveAddress */ ControllerInitiated, /* SlaveMode */ 400000, /* ConnectionSpeed */ AddressingMode7Bit, /* AddressingMode */ "\\_SB.I2C1", /* ResourceSource */ ) GpioInt (Edge, ActiveLow, ExclusiveAndWake, PullNone,, "\\_SB.GPSW") { BOARD_TOUCH_GPIO_INDEX } } ) Return (BUF0) } ... } This gives troubles with drivers such as Elan Touchscreen driver (elants_i2c) that uses devm_gpiod_get to look up "reset" GPIO line and decide whether the driver is responsible for powering up and resetting the device, or firmware is. In the above case the lookup succeeds, we map GPIO as output and later fail to request client->irq interrupt that is mapped to the same GPIO. Let's ignore resources described as GpioInt() while parsing _CRS when requesting output GPIOs (but allow them when requesting GPIOD_ASIS or GPIOD_IN as some drivers, such as i2c-hid, do request GPIO as input and then map it to interrupt with gpiod_to_irq). Acked-by: Mika Westerberg <mika.westerberg@linux.intel.com> Signed-off-by: Dmitry Torokhov <dtor@chromium.org> Signed-off-by: Linus Walleij <linus.walleij@linaro.org> BUG=chrome-os-partner:61233 TEST=Build and boot (cherry picked from commit 25487533ff311014b0cc39ed7fd721c114e1b11f) Change-Id: I0d8d8148965f58954bfbb65b87240133df5daefd Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/444147 Commit-Ready: Dmitry Torokhov <dtor@chromium.org> Tested-by: Dmitry Torokhov <dtor@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Furquan Shaikh <furquan@chromium.org>

instalog: output_archive: lower memory usage Although creating archives in-memory could be considered a "cleaner" and "safer" solution, problems were encountered when creating large archives (~200mb). Python memory usage was skyrocketing to the point that the kernel would kill the Instalog process. Thus we modify output_archive to instead output to a directory on disk. Once the directory is fully prepared, we create an archive based on its contents. Also add a unittest, including a test for memory usage. instalog: make socket plugin more durable We were encountering a problem on slow network connections: (1) OUTPUT send returns immediately (2) OUTPUT blocks waiting for success-failure response (3) INPUT recv calls total longer than _SOCKET_TIMEOUT (but each individual call is still within the timeout) (4) OUTPUT times out since it waits > _SOCKET_TIMEOUT, marks the batch of events as failed (5) INPUT commits the batch of events (6) INPUT sends success-failure response, but realizes the other side of the socket is down (7) OUTPUT re-sends the same batch of events (continue from (1)) This process could repeat a couple times, causing quite a lot of duplicate events. The solution for this is to add a final syn/ack/syn-ack confirmation sequence: SYN: OUTPUT has received the data and is ready to emit it. ACK: INPUT is still standing by, and requests the emit. SYN-ACK: OUTPUT reports the success/failure of the emit call. BUG=None TEST=Manually on local machine Change-Id: I74433d50c76e0fb85d310b17f605e49014a5b8a0 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/434437 Commit-Ready: Joel Kitching <kitching@chromium.org> Tested-by: Joel Kitching <kitching@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Chih-Yu Huang <akahuang@chromium.org>

Follow change in flashrom r1579 Before r1579 struct flashctx contains copies of various fields from struct flashchip. That commit changed flashctx to hold a pointer to a flashchip instead. For this, many uses of flashctx need to be adapted, and this commit follows this change (which doesn't apply cleanly due to the divergence between trees). This commit was created in 3 steps: 1. Replace these fields in struct flashctx with struct flashchip *chip; 2. Apply the following coccinelle semantic patch: @@ struct flashctx var; @@ -var. +var.chip-> ( vendor \| name \| bustype \| manufacture_id \| model_id \| total_size \| page_size \| feature_bits \| tested \| probe \| probe_timing \| block_erasers \| printlock \| unlock \| write \| read \| read_status \| write_status \| voltage \| wp ) @@ struct flashctx *varptr; @@ -varptr-> +varptr->chip-> ( vendor \| name \| bustype \| manufacture_id \| model_id \| total_size \| page_size \| feature_bits \| tested \| probe \| probe_timing \| block_erasers \| printlock \| unlock \| write \| read \| read_status \| write_status \| voltage \| wp ) 3. Adapt flashrom.c probe_flash() needs to be adapted to fill in struct flashctx->chip instead of assuming that flashctx contains the same set of fields. g: rate limit firmware updates This patch introduces a delay between accepted cr50 firmware upload attempts. The next attempt to write into the same or lower address in flash would be accepted no sooner than in 60 seconds after the previous attempt. This would prevent a rogue user from wearing the flash by repeated uploads to the same address. This limitation is not imposed by dev images (those compiled with CR50_DEV=1). BRANCH=none BUG=chrome-os-partner:63098 TEST=verified that attempts to update soon after the previous update result in the following error message issued by usb_updater: sending 0x2d8b8 bytes to 0x4000 Error: status 0x9 Modified usb_updater to send one random pdu twice. Observed the same error message. Change-Id: Idca55ad091d09daaddd0a4cad5b1f871af1ede93 Signed-off-by: Vadim Bendebury <vbendeb@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/445496 Reviewed-by: Mary Ruthven <mruthven@chromium.org>

UPSTREAM: packet: round up linear to header len [ Upstream commit 57031eb794906eea4e1c7b31dc1e2429c0af0c66 ] Link layer protocols may unconditionally pull headers, as Ethernet does in eth_type_trans. Ensure that the entire link layer header always lies in the skb linear segment. tpacket_snd has such a check. Extend this to packet_snd. Variable length link layer headers complicate the computation somewhat. Here skb->len may be smaller than dev->hard_header_len. Round up the linear length to be at least as long as the smallest of the two. CHROMIUM: Consider min_free_kbytes in low memory notification. The parameter min_free_kbytes controls low watermark. Memory under low watermark is reserved for emergency page allocation. A regular page allocation could not use them. As a result, the reserved memory should not be considered available when checking memory status. BUG=chromium:645512 TEST=System functions normally and passed autotest cheets_LowMemoryKiller. shill: vpn: fix external task cleanup in L2TPIPSecDriver Upon termination of the 'l2tpipsec_vpn' external task launched by L2TPIPSecDriver, the following callback sequence is invoked, which leads to the destruction of the ExternalTask instance during the invocation of ExternalTask::OnTaskDied(): ExternalTask::OnTaskDied() -> L2TPIPSecDriver::OnL2TPIPSecVPNDied() -> L2TPIPSecDriver::FailService() -> L2TPIPSecDriver::Cleanup() -> ExternalTask::~ExternalTask() This CL changes the code to use ExternalTask::DestroyLater() to mitigate the issue. BUG=chromium:656410 TEST=Run unit tests. TEST=Run network_VPNConnect autotest. nvmem: do not prefer old partition over new one. The code deciding which partition to choose properly determines which one is newer, but invariably populates the cache with the second one, when both partitions are valid. This is obviously wrong, on top of that there is no need to check both partitions' validity, if the newer one checks out. install_toolchain: do not die if ${toolchain}/go is not installed. Having go installed as part of a toolchain was always optional. install_toolchain_in_provided() function has a check if $go_ver is empty, and only adds go to package.provided if it's not. Unfortunately, cross_get_version() was dying if go is not found. I've split cross_get_version() into two functions. The original cross_get_version() does not die if the package is not found. A new function cross_get_version_or_die() checks the results and dies if the package was not found. Checking go version uses cross_get_version(). Checking gcc/glibc version uses cross_get_version_or_die(). BUG=None TEST='setup_board --board=x86-zgb' works after disabling i686-pc-linux-gnu-go in cl/444042. Change-Id: Ice92e2c8a5a91ff474f2f3a35b8d6b2be0d92a5c Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/444043 Commit-Ready: Rahul Chaudhry <rahulchaudhry@chromium.org> Tested-by: Rahul Chaudhry <rahulchaudhry@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Luis Lozano <llozano@chromium.org>
